name: Solenne Neuralcrest Lattice Fascinator II
description:
A sculptural Spire-tier fascinator built around exposed neural-port hardware as the centerpiece of the design. The base is hand-formed iridescent bioresin — shifting from deep violet to pale gold depending on angle — mounted on a swept platinum wire frame that clips invisibly into the hair or scalp anchors. Radiating from the port hub, articulated filaments of gold-tone chromalloy wire extend in an asymmetric lattice, tipped with micro-droplets of cultured bioluminescent pearl.

The piece actively integrates with BCI hardware: the lattice filaments carry passive signal-routing capacity, functioning as a short-range social BCI relay while broadcasting the wearer's preferred public identity tag to nearby compatible devices. Couture-made. No two are identical.
functionality: Passive BCI social relay via chromalloy lattice: broadcasts identity tag, preferred contact protocols, and status tier to nearby BCI-enabled individuals. Scalp-anchor mounting is compatible with port-adjacent chrome hardware. Bioluminescent pearl elements glow faintly in low light without power draw.
what_it_says: Your neural hardware is not hidden — it is the jewel, and everyone in the room is already receiving your signal.
worn_by: elite social figures with visible BCI hardware
story_hooks: A Solenne Lattice II was found in a Tier 2 pawn shop — the identity tag still broadcast, and it belongs to someone officially listed as deceased.
The passive relay function has an undocumented secondary mode: it logs every BCI identifier within six meters, and Solenne's data arm has been quietly selling the records.
A Spire gala guest's fascinator began broadcasting a distress-coded identity tag mid-event — no one in the room admitted to noticing, but three people left early.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sculptural crown-like fascinator that frames the wearer's head with an asymmetric halo of articulated wire filaments. The exposed neural port sits as the dramatic focal point, surrounded by a swept platinum wire armature and radiating golden chromalloy lattice. The bioresin base catches light and shifts color with movement. Reads as haute couture augmentation jewelry rather than traditional headwear.
physical_description.fit: Custom-fitted to individual scalp anatomy; mounts via invisible hair clips or direct scalp anchor ports. Lightweight despite visual impact. Sits high and proud on the crown, extending laterally and backward in an asymmetric sweep.
physical_description.primary_material: Hand-formed iridescent bioresin base, platinum wire frame, gold-tone chromalloy filaments, cultured bioluminescent pearl micro-droplets, exposed neural-port hardware
physical_description.texture: Smooth, lustrous bioresin with subtle depth and opalescence. Delicate articulated wire filaments with a brushed metallic finish. Pearl tips catch light with soft bioluminescence. Smooth where it contacts skin.
physical_description.color_scheme: Iridescent bioresin shifting violet-to-gold depending on viewing angle. Platinum and gold-tone metallics. Warm bioluminescent pearls (cream-white with subtle glow). High contrast between glossy resin and brushed metal.
physical_description.closures: Invisible friction-fit hair clips or direct scalp port integration; no visible mechanical fasteners
distinctive_features: Articulated chromalloy filaments with bioluminescent pearl tips
Iridescent bioresin that color-shifts with angle
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1 luxury — haute couture neural augmentation jewelry at Spire level. Five to six-figure Φ price point.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by elite corporate consciousness-jockeys, high-society BCI enthusiasts, and augmentation fashionistas who view neural ports as aesthetic statements. Signals wealth, cutting-edge biotech integration, and willingness to broadcast identity intentionally. Corpo socialite to high-end rogue consciousness explorer.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine to museum-quality when new; aged pieces show subtle micro-scratches on chrome filaments and slight dulling of pearl luminescence. Each piece gains character over years of use. Never salvaged or mass-produced.
